title: The Poisoned Pawn
summary: Grandmaster Viktor Petrov collapses during Game 7 of the World Chess Championship in Vienna. Thallium poison in his thermos.
briefing: Vienna, October 1986. Cold War tensions simmer. In the Grand Hotel Ballroom, 2,000 spectators watch Game 7 of the World Chess Championship between Soviet champion Viktor Petrov and challenger Alexei Volkov. On move 34, Viktor reaches for his silver thermos, sips his herbal tea, and collapses. Thallium poisoning. He lies in a coma at Vienna General Hospital. Was this Soviet state sabotage, private extortion, or personal vengeance?

locations.name: World Championship Stage
locations.description: The chess board remains frozen mid-game. Turn 34: Queen's Gambit Declined. The silver thermos sits knocked over on the green felt table.

hotspots.name: Viktor's Silver Thermos
hotspots.description: Police toxicology reveals high concentration of odorless Thallium sulfate mixed into green herbal tea.

hotspots.name: Official Match Score Sheet
hotspots.description: Viktor had played a brilliant novel move on turn 32, forcing opponent Alexei Volkov into imminent checkmate.

locations.name: Viktor's Hotel Suite (Room 402)
locations.description: Luxurious suite with views of the Vienna Opera House. Chess books and travel luggage scattered about.

suspects.name: Natasha Petrov
suspects.description: 38, Viktor's wife and business manager. Sitting stiffly on the sofa.

dialogueOptions.text: Who had access to Viktor's silver thermos before the match?
dialogueOptions.response: Only Ivan, his official KGB trainer and handler! Ivan prepares Viktor's tea every afternoon in the suite kitchen without fail.

dialogueOptions.text: We found two Austrian passports with fake names in your safe.
dialogueOptions.response: Yes! Viktor and I were planning to defect to the West right after winning Game 7! We had US Embassy asylum papers hidden in his jacket!

hotspots.name: Hidden Wall Safe
hotspots.description: Two forged Austrian passports and a stamped letter of political asylum from the US Embassy in Vienna.

locations.name: Hotel Grand Lounge Bar
locations.description: Dim jazz lounge, crystal chandeliers, smoke hanging in the air.

suspects.name: Klaus Eberhardt
suspects.description: 52, Tournament Organizer & Austrian Sports Minister. Sipping cognac.

dialogueOptions.text: Rumor says you placed heavy bets on Alexei Volkov winning the title.
dialogueOptions.response: I am the organizer! I bet on excitement! But poisoning my own star player would ruin me financially!

dialogueOptions.text: You had a private meeting with Viktor in this bar last night.
dialogueOptions.response: He promised me the exclusive story of his Western defection! He knew his handler Ivan was watching him closely.

hotspots.name: Corner Booth Ashtray
hotspots.description: Matches from the Soviet Embassy and a crumpled code telegram reading: 'PREVENT DEFECTION AT ALL COSTS.'

locations.name: International Press Center
locations.description: Typewriters clacking, telegraph wires buzzing with global sports coverage.

suspects.name: Ivan Krasnov
suspects.description: 50, Official Soviet Team Trainer & Handler. Cold eyes, military posture.

dialogueOptions.text: Did you prepare Viktor's tea before today's match?
dialogueOptions.response: I prepare comrade Viktor's tea every day at 13:00. It is standard physical conditioning routine.

dialogueOptions.text: We found the Soviet Embassy telegram ordering Viktor's defection stopped.
dialogueOptions.response: Comrade Viktor was a hero of the state! He would never defect... unless treasonous forces corrupted him.

hotspots.name: Trash Can behind Soviet Desk
hotspots.description: An empty glass ampoule labeled 'Thallium Sulfate - Moscow Chemical Works Depot #4'.

locations.name: Backstage Green Room
locations.description: Private rest area for players between games.

suspects.name: Alexei Volkov
suspects.description: 26, Challenger Grandmaster. Looking shaken and exhausted.

dialogueOptions.text: Did you know Viktor was winning Game 7?
dialogueOptions.response: He was destroying my defense! But I wanted to defeat him on the 64 squares! Poisoning him destroys my reputation forever!

hotspots.name: Ivan's Lockbox
hotspots.description: Duplicate key to Viktor's thermos and a pair of rubber gloves stained with liquid Thallium traces.

solution.explanation: Ivan Krasnov, official Soviet team handler and state agent, discovered Viktor Petrov was defecting to the West with US Embassy asylum papers. Following explicit Soviet Embassy telegram orders to 'prevent defection at all costs,' Ivan used his exclusive access to prepare Viktor's herbal tea, dosing the silver thermos with Moscow Chemical Thallium sulfate prior to Game 7.
